issues.description: PersonService.addParent(Person, Person) is specified and provided in the template as a public method, and it is called from PersonResource. In the solution, addParent(Person, Person) is implemented as private, which would prevent PersonResource (another class) from compiling against PersonService.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution method signature to `public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent)` (keeping the same parameters/return type). If a helper is desired, introduce a separate private helper and have the public method delegate to it.

issues.description: The problem statement suggests making start.sh executable using `chmod 700 start.sh`, but the solution Dockerfile uses `chmod 770 start.sh`. While both make the script executable, the differing permission mode can confuse students about what is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Either change the solution to `RUN chmod 700 start.sh` or update the problem statement to a permission-agnostic instruction such as `chmod +x start.sh`.

issues.description: The exercise instructs students to put their own (globally unique) Heroku app name into heroku-app-name.txt. The solution repository contains a concrete value ("H10E01-Containers"), which can mislead students into thinking the app name must match the repository/project name.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep heroku-app-name.txt empty or use a clear placeholder (e.g., `<your-heroku-app-name>`), and ensure documentation/tests do not imply it must equal the project name.
